facts.claim: Creek Bay is registered with the Dubai Land Department as project 4198, with buyer payments going to that project's registered escrow account.
The DLD-registered completion date is 30 April 2030.
Agents and portals describe completion in Q2 2030 or April 2030, and one says "handover in 2030".
A June 2026 update reports certified progress of 0.62%, with enabling works under way.
Creek Bay is a three-tower waterfront complex of one- to three-bedroom apartments by Emaar Properties.
facts.value: three towers of 1 to 3 bedroom apartments

facts.claim: Launch prices are described as starting around AED 1.8 million; resale prices may differ from launch prices.
Apartments in Dubai Creek Harbour transacted at around AED 2,600 per sq ft in January to June 2026, against AED 3,011 in Downtown Dubai, according to DLD data reported by a property site.
One agent describes an 80/20 plan: 10% down payment and seven equal instalments to completion.
Another agent describes a 10/70/20 plan: 10% at launch, 70% during construction and 20% at handover.

facts.field: master developer of Dubai Creek Harbour
facts.claim: One source describes Dubai Creek Harbour as a master plan by Emaar Properties and Dubai Holding.

facts.field: master developer of Dubai Creek Harbour
facts.claim: Another describes Emaar as the sole master developer.
A competitor's guide says Emaar has never cancelled a Dubai Creek Harbour project and typically delivers within six months of the stated date.
Off-plan sales in Dubai are registered on the DLD's Oqood system, which makes the purchase an official record; a registration fee is payable to the DLD.

Under Dubai Law 19 of 2017, if a buyer defaults and the unit is less than 60% complete, the developer may cancel the contract and keep up to 25% of the price, returning the rest within a year or within 60 days of resale; between 60% and 80%, up to 40%; above 80%, it may also hold the buyer to the contract or seek an auction.

Before acting on a default, the developer must notify the DLD, which gives the buyer 30 days and then certifies the percentage of completion; buyers may still go to court or arbitration if the developer abuses these powers.
